steps.body:
The first term is \(a=k+2\) and the common difference is \(d=3\).

Successive listed terms differ by 3.
steps.title: Solution | Step 1

steps.body:
\[S_n=\frac n2\{2(k+2)+3(n-1)\}=\frac n2(2k+1+3n).\]

Apply the arithmetic-series sum formula.
steps.title: Solution | Step 2

steps.body:
\[S_{2n}=n\{2(k+2)+3(2n-1)\}=n(2k+1+6n).\]

Use 2n in place of n throughout the sum formula.
steps.title: Solution | Step 3

steps.body:
Using \(S_{2n}=4S_n\) and \(n>0\), \[2k+1+6n=2(2k+1+3n)=4k+2+6n.\]

Divide the equation by n, then expand the right-hand side.
steps.title: Solution | Step 4

steps.body:
\[2k+1=4k+2\quad\Rightarrow\quad k=-\frac12.\]

The n-terms cancel, leaving a linear equation for k.
steps.title: Solution | Step 5

steps.body:
\[u_{100}=k+2+99(3)=-\frac12+2+297=298.5.\]

The 100th term is the first term plus 99 common differences.
